Equipment:
 Differential 
 Protection Relay
 KBCH 130
 GEC

The KBCH relay provides a package of functions primarily for the 
protection of transformers and generator transformers but may also be applied to 
protect reactors and generators. As a part of the K-range of relays, the KBCH 
can be integrated into an overall protection and control system by utilizing its 
integral serial communications facility. Winding KBCH130 offers 3 bias inputs 
per phase for all applications requiring up to 3 bias circuits.

All models are available with either 1A or 5A inputs on the primary 
and secondary side. Alternatively thumbs 120 and 140 can be provided with 1A 
CT's on the high voltage windings and 5A CT's on the low voltage windings. for 
 Auto transformers or, generator- transformer units the KBCH is suitable and 
also for other applications where biased differential protection is appropriate 
(e.g. generators, reactors and motors).All models are three phase units with 
internal vector group compensation and line current transformer ratio 
correction, thus eliminating the need for interposing transformers in most 
cases.

This procedure details the steps required to completely check the 
proper operation and calibration of the KBCH130 relay. It is recommended this 
procedure be carried out on an annually bases

The document is formatted the 
way to minimize the possibility of error causing personal injury or damage to 
equipment.

Review the manual and drawings.
Carefully follow these test procedure steps
Check the wires of the relay by hand.
Check the AC source is available to the tester.
Check the existence of the DC sources in panels.

Disconnect the trip leads of the relay and connect one of them to the timer of 
 the tester.
Check all the leads used in tests.

Verify the test results match the relay setting - If not consult technical 
 services.

Make sure CT secondary circuits are shorted at the incoming terminal blocks 
 before isolating the relay current circuits for test.

Look at field maintenance file and compare the position of the setting 
 switches on relay with those shown in the setting sheet.

Switch off the DC power supply and make sure that 
 Terminals (3 & 5) are closed and Terminals (4 & 6) are open.

Switch on the DC power supply and make sure that 
 Terminals (3 & 5) are open and Terminals (4 & 6) are closed.

This test to check the operation of the output 
 relays

Go to the TEST/ CONTROL menu heading and step down 
 until the [select relay for test] cell is displayed.

Each bit in this cell corresponds to an output 
 relay. Bit 0 for relay 0 bit 1 for relay 1 and so on.

Select one relay at a time by setting the 
 appropriate bit to 1. Then, step down one to the [Test Relays = [0]] cell.

The output relay will close for the duration that 
 the [0] key is pressed plus the time set in the cell [LOG to Test] which is 
 found under the menu heading LOGIC FUNCTIONS.

All bits must be returned back to be ones after 
 check

Inject current into the relay and increase it to 
 reach 5Amp with frequency 50Hz to HV,LV1 and LV2 sides

Take the reading of Phase current, Differential 
 Current and Bias Current from LCD display.
Record the values on the test sheet.
Repeat these steps for phase B and C

items:
Connect test lead between the current terminal on 
 the relay for phase A as shown in drawing from the HV side and the current 
 terminals on the test set.

Slowly increase the current until the red LED 
 lights. The relay must operate with a current between +/- 10% of the setting 
 value.
Record this value on the test sheet.
Slowly decrease the current until the LED reset.
Record this value on the test sheet.
Repeat these steps for phase B and C
Repeat these steps for LV1 side and LV2 side

Inject current into the relay from HV side and 
 increase it to reach (5 Is) . Keep this value and switch off the test set.

Connect the relay trip output contacts to the timer 
 contacts of the test set.

Switch on the test set and inject current. The timer 
 will stop instantaneous (30 to 40 msec).
Record this value on the test sheet.
Repeat these steps for phase B and C

Request the operator to switch on the main circuit 
 breaker.

Operate the output auxiliary contact by injection to 
 trip the circuit breaker.
Check that the circuit breaker tripped.

sections.text: Return the Relay and Power Equipment to Service

items: Clear the fault recorder data.

Verify the test result match the relay setting. If 
 not consult technical services.

Test trip the circuit breaker associated with the 
 relay.

Make a final check that all switches on the relay 
 are set according to the setting sheet.

Make sure the CT secondary circuit is in normal 
 condition

Remove the CT shorts which were installed in the 
 Power Supply
Return the relay and power equipment to service.
